name: esm
title: Exploitation State Machine states
definition: The condition an offense is in: what it has reached, and the leverage it holds. Milestones are the states of the machine; tracks say how a milestone was reached. Each state is reached from evidence, never from the offense's domain.

terminals.Completed: The goal was reached, whether or not the offense was later detected.
terminals.Disrupted: Detection is narrated before the goal was reached.
terminals.Unresolved: The telling ends before the goal, with no detection narrated.

states.definition: Means are set up: accounts, identities, infrastructure, tools. No victim has been reached.
A victim, a person or a system, has been reached.
The offender holds leverage over the victim before anything is taken: a false belief, a demand, a threat, control.
Value or a person has been taken, or the offense's harm delivered.
Leverage is held again after exploitation, so the offense can continue.
After exploitation, proceeds are moved or traces concealed.
A person is approached by the offender: a call, a message, a meeting.
A person is enlisted with an offer: work, travel, a relationship.
A computer system or account is entered without authority.
The victim cooperates under a false belief the offender induced: a pretext, a false identity, a false promise.
The victim complies under a threat of harm or the offender's control of their movement, documents, money or communication. Once held, coercion is not undone by a later deception.
Money, property or data has passed from the victim to the offender.
Labor, sex or images have been taken from the person.
Contraband has been supplied to buyers. Harm is delivered, but no victim is the source of what the offender gains.
Proceeds are moved, converted or placed after exploitation.
Traces of the offense are hidden or destroyed after exploitation.
